=========================================================================
HANDOFF — /rebar-implement on epic e369 (adroit-deductible-kakapo). READ FIRST.
=========================================================================

## Where things stand

EPIC e369 in_progress. 4 of 8 stories CLOSED this session (J1 was already done at pickup):
  J1 acb2 CLOSED + MERGED (change 1009 -> commit 7fc96b277, now origin/main)
  J2 62d9 CLOSED — change 1010, LLM-Review +1 / Verified +1, submittable
  J4 0a94 CLOSED — change 1011 PS2, both gates green
  J3 aac8 CLOSED — change 1013 PS4, both gates green
  J5 c97f OPEN, UNCLAIMED — BLOCKED ON HARDWARE (see below)
  J6 9fd4 / J7 b4e3 / J8 8c35 — still blocked; J6 needs J4 AND J5, so the chain stops at J5.

## The stack — NOT YET LANDED, deliberately

  1009 (J1, MERGED) <- 1010 (J2) <- 1011 (J4) <- 1013 (J3)
All three open changes are green on BOTH gates with 0 unresolved comments and submittable=True.
Per the skill, the stack lands together after the EPIC closes; the epic cannot close while J5-J8 are open. So
1010/1011/1013 are intentionally parked, green, on branch jira-family-seam in /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-jira-family
(HEAD = J3's PS4 commit). An operator who wants them on main now can submit 1013 (submitting the top of a
stack submits its ancestors) — they are independently green and each was closed on its own evidence.

## Why J5 is blocked (hardware, not plan, not code)

The harness needs a real Jira 8.17.1 at localhost:2990. THREE runs on this host:
  1. plain entrypoint -> died ~25min: Cargo 'failed to finish deploying within the timeout period [600000]'.
  2. -DstartupTimeout / -Dcargo.timeout -> died identically; those property names have NO effect.
  3. -Dproduct.start.timeout=2700000 (from Atlassian docs) -> NO watchdog kill in 55 min, so this IS the right
     property, but it never reached Jira startup. The base image is linux/amd64 and this host is arm64;
     EMULATION is the wall, not configuration.
J5's AC1/AC2 require the readiness probe to report REST answering and a smoke test to create+read an issue.
Unsatisfiable here. I did NOT claim it — claiming to author unverifiable files would hide unproven work behind
a green board. NEEDED: a native amd64 runner.

## J5's PLAN is now materially better than at pickup — that IS this session's J5 deliverable

Its plan-review had PASSED with a FALSE PREMISE. Fixed, all verified against primary sources:
 * 'pinned, PULLABLE image pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1' is FICTION — docker pull says 'repository does
   not exist'; Hub API says object not found; the pycontribs namespace has 7 repos, all OS base images. The tag
   is a LOCAL BUILD NAME (upstream ships docker/jira-test-image/Dockerfile; its README says docker build).
   Base addono/jira-software-standalone IS pullable and the pinned digest resolves. Plan now says BUILD.
   ALSO FIXED THE SAME CLAIM IN THE EPIC (step 5) — I had corrected the child and left the parent lying.
 * The image does NOT contain Jira: atlas-run downloads it from maven.atlassian.com at runtime (~917
   artifacts). So egress to Atlassian is a RUNTIME dependency and PINNING THE DIGEST DOES NOT PIN JIRA.
 * Tier corrected from 'integration' to 'external'. CRITICAL: _build-and-test.yml runs 'pytest -m integration'
   as its OWN step on every commit (those tests 'need no live services'), so the integration marker is an
   INCLUSION into CI — Docker-requiring tests there break CI for everyone. tests/external/ is the genuinely
   fenced tier (conftest auto-marks it and hard-fails misplacement; runs only from external-integration.yml on
   dispatch/weekly cron).
 * Enumerated the external tier's INHERITED contract: the _require_external_opt_in autouse fixture skips
   everything without REBAR_RUN_EXTERNAL=1; the _live_jira_ready sentinel drives the jira_live marker and the
   all-skip canary (the new smoke module MUST define it or a silently-all-skipped run looks green); settled
   skip-vs-fail (absent harness => SKIP + actionable message; the CANARY, not a hard failure, prevents vacuous
   green — a hard failure would break the pre-existing external CI job that has no Docker).
 * external-integration.yml enumerated as needing its OWN amd64 job (it already collects tests/external/ and
   has no docker steps, and gates on an LLM key this harness does not need).
 * -Dproduct.start.timeout recorded as the correct AMPS property WITH the failure it prevents, so nobody
   deletes it; -DstartupTimeout/-Dcargo.timeout recorded as NOT working so nobody repeats my two wasted runs.
 * Also fixed: Makefile:154 -> 178 (154 is inside actionlint-bin); .PHONY:30 needs jira-dc-up; 'ADR 0037 §3'
   was unresolvable (FIVE files share that prefix) -> named 0037-reconciler-live-validation-harness.md;
   loopback-scoped port; programmatic PAT via POST /rest/pat/latest/tokens; 20-min readiness default; the
   'carries its own license' claim REMOVED as unverified.
 * REMOVED an AC I had wrongly added: allow_insecure is J6's deliverable (J6 already carries it), and J5's
   smoke tests speak raw REST and never touch rebar config. It made an 'independently claimable' story depend
   on J6. Recorded why so nobody restores it.
J5's last review pass: 5 blocking, all addressed in the current text; it needs ONE more review-plan run.

## Tickets FILED for real defects found

 65d7-8270-bdc6-41f6 (impious-safe-bettong) — the outbound mapper's _assignee_resolver is injected by ATTRIBUTE
   and read via getattr with a silent non-authoritative fallback. discovered_from J4. Removing it needs the
   backend-neutral port signature to change (wider blast radius than J4's 3-file scope).
 2bc7-d77b-641c-42aa (unrelative-inbred-piglet) — test helpers call sys.modules.setdefault but RETURN the newly
   created module, so five files racing on the 'mutation' key hand back a class that is not the registered one
   and isinstance fails. THIS CAUSED J4's Verified -1 on macos-py3.13 while ubuntu-py3.13 passed. Fixed inside
   J4 (had to sit at/below it) and DISCLOSED in that commit message. discovered_from J4.

## Environment

Worktree /Users/joeoakhart/rebar-jira-family, branch jira-family-seam, clean, HEAD = J3 PS4.
All Jira probe containers + the m2 volume + my two throwaway images REMOVED. Kept only
pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1 (879MB) so a later amd64 attempt skips the ~900-artifact download; delete
with 'docker rmi pycontribs/jira-test-image:8.17.1'.

## Immediate next actions

 1. J5 on a NATIVE AMD64 host: run 'rebar review-plan c97f' (expect PASS or few blockers), claim, implement.
 2. Then J6 (unblocks once J4+J5 closed) -> J7 -> J8, each via the same held-out TDD loop.
 3. Land the stack by submitting the top change once the epic closes — or submit 1013 now if the operator wants
    the four finished stories on main without waiting for J5-J8.

## Gate/tooling lessons worth carrying (all cost me time)

 * A same-tree 'git commit --amend --no-edit' does NOT re-trigger the LLM review: Gerrit COPIES the votes
   ('same tree ... Copied Votes'). A coverage-gap -1 needs a REAL tree change (or a maintainer re-trigger).
   'recheck' re-runs CI ONLY — every recheck reference in the docs is about Verified.
 * 'git commit --amend -F <file>' REGENERATES the Change-Id unless the message already contains it — this
   orphaned change 1008 in the previous session and nearly orphaned 1011 here. Always diff trailers before push.
 * A blank line between trailers splits the block so %(trailers) drops rebar-ticket. Keep them contiguous.
 * Do NOT read a test suite whose files changed mid-run. I killed one 30-min run for that and re-ran it.
 * Do NOT run an emulated JVM beside the suite — this repo has wall-clock-sensitive tests.
 * VERIFY a mutation actually applied. One of mine was a silent no-op that 'passed' 14 tests and proved nothing.
